comment: The derived Bearer name for a hosted connector. Python owns the rule in packages/plugin-format/src/plugin_format/connector_render.py::_derived_headers; the Rust CLI hand-mirrors it as bearer_secret_name in cli/src/connector_build.rs. The two cannot share code across languages, so the cases are frozen here. Each vector is a connectors.yaml document with one hosted connector named gh. expected_name is the secret the derived Authorization: Bearer ${NAME} header expands, or null when no header is derived. Python asserts mcp_entry headers match; Rust asserts bearer_secret_name matches. Changing one language without this file fails that language; editing this file without the other language fails the other suite. Both lanes reject unknown vector keys so a key added for one side cannot pass vacuously on the other.

vectors.name: explicit-bearer-secret
vectors.why: explicit bearer_secret wins even when several secrets are declared

vectors.name: single-plain-string-secret
vectors.why: the github-mcp-server shape: one plain string secret is the Bearer name

vectors.name: single-secret-ref
vectors.why: an implicit lone SecretRef does not derive a Bearer header; its value never reaches the sandbox

vectors.name: two-secrets
vectors.why: two secrets and no bearer_secret derive nothing rather than picking secrets[0]; validation already refuses this with connectors.bearer_secret_required, so this pins the defense-in-depth answer
